verdict.rationale: Concurrency caps per pricing tier, and the cost to raise them, are a fair question for web-crawling products, so the axis applies. Crawl4AI's evidence only describes it as open source with "no paywalls" and mentions parallel crawling. Nothing documents pricing tiers, per-tier concurrent session or request limits, or any cost to raise a cap.

support.subject: As a data-engineer, I know the maximum concurrent sessions or requests allowed on my pricing tier and the cost to raise that cap
